summary.text: Jim Mehlhaff is a Republican state senator from South Dakota's District 24 who took office on January 10, 2023, and has served as Senate majority leader since January 15, 2025.
He advanced from the June 2, 2026, Republican primary and is seeking re-election in the November 3 general election.

paragraphs.text: Mehlhaff's career experience, according to Ballotpedia, includes owning a business and working in state government, and he served on the St. Joseph School Board.
Ballotpedia also lists him as a member of the Pierre City Commission from 2009 to 2021.
Mehlhaff first won the District 24 seat in 2022, when he defeated incumbent Mary Duvall in the Republican primary, 3,157 votes to 3,003, and then won the general election unopposed.
In the 2025-2026 session he chairs the Senate State Affairs Committee and is vice chair of the Senate Legislative Procedure Committee; he also serves on the Senate Judiciary Committee.
In the 2026 Republican primary he defeated Brian Murphy and Mark Nelson, receiving 54.4% of the vote.
